subject: Clarify DPA: subprocessor access, output ownership & model-improvement opt-out
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <s.martinez@novumhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Novum Legal <legal@novumhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: DPA clarification: model improvement and subprocessor evidence

Hi Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed the proposed DPA and has two outstanding asks we need to resolve before procurement can sign:

1) No-model-improvement commitment: Novum needs explicit contractual language that our customer data (prompts, responses, logs) will not be used to improve any third-party models. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a firm "no-model-improvement" covenant and if there are differences across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.

2) Subprocessor access & evidence: we require a subprocessor matrix and an auditable statement confirming that subprocessors do not retain prompt/response content beyond transient processing. If possible, we also need an export of any access logs or attestations showing no retention for our tenant.

Attached are our redlines for reference (Novum_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf). Please advise what evidence you can provide and a realistic timeline.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Martinez
Head of Compliance, Novum Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <s.martinez@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA clarification: model improvement and subprocessor evidence

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Quick summary and next steps from our side: 

- No-model-improvement commitment: Redwood can accept a contractual "no-model-improvement" (no training / no persistent use for model improvement) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API customers we offer an enterprise opt-out toggle that prevents tenant data from being used for model improvement; we can add an explicit contract clause and operational attestations for your org.

- Subprocessor evidence: we will provide a current subprocessor matrix and a short evidence pack (attestation + access-log export showing no retention for your tenant) within 3–5 business days after legal confirms the request scope.

- Output / IP ownership: our standard DPA already states customers retain ownership of prompts and generated outputs. We'll add an explicit sentence referencing "prompt/response ownership" for clarity in the redline version.

I've looped in Rishi (security/compliance) to prepare the evidence pack and Marissa (AE) to coordinate the contract redlines and DocuSign flow. Expect the evidence pack by end of next week.

If you want the strongest guarantees we can put the no-training commitment and the evidence deliverables into the SOW or an addendum tied to your Dedicated instance. Happy to discuss.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference

Hi all — Rishi from Security here. Attaching the list of items we can provide and the expected delivery cadence: 

Deliverables (we will provide as PDFs / CSVs):
- Current subprocessor matrix (names, roles, locations) — attached as subprocessor_matrix.xlsx.
- Data flow diagram for Novum deployment (tenant isolation, network controls).
- Access-log extract showing no long-term retention of prompt/response data for tenant "Novum Health" (time-bounded export).
- Operational attestation signed by our Head of Privacy confirming we do not use Novum prompts/responses for model improvement for this tenant.
- SOC 2 Type II report pointer and redaction guidance where applicable.

Notes on deployments:
- Dedicated / Private: customer data never leaves the customer's environment by default; we can contractually guarantee no model-improvement usage and provide the attestation.
- Hosted: we support an enterprise-level opt-out flag that prevents tenant data from entering any model-improvement pipelines and can be documented in the DPA. There is an operational audit trail for toggles and for processing flows.

IP / outputs: our legal team confirms the standard DPA grants customers ownership of prompts and generated outputs; we will add a single-sentence clarification to the redline: "Customer retains all intellectual property rights in prompts and generated outputs; Redwood shall not assert ownership or use such data to derive model weights or improvements."

Timeline: we will assemble the evidence pack (matrix + attestation + access-log extract) and share via a secure link within 3 business days after receiving signed NDA scope or a confirmation email from Novum Legal on the specific export window.

Attachments: subprocessor_matrix.xlsx

— Rishi
